welch_t_test.name: Welch's Two-Sample t-Test (Weather Impact on Delay Duration)
welch_t_test.null_hypothesis: H0: True mean arrival delay in adverse weather equals mean arrival delay in clear weather (mu_bad = mu_clear)
welch_t_test.alt_hypothesis: H1: True mean arrival delay in adverse weather is greater than in clear weather (mu_bad > mu_clear)
welch_t_test.conclusion: Arrival delay duration is significantly higher during adverse weather conditions (p < 0.0001).

two_prop_z_test.name: Two-Proportion z-Test (Evening Congestion vs Morning OTP)
two_prop_z_test.null_hypothesis: H0: The proportion of delayed flights in evening peak (17:00-21:00) equals morning departures (06:00-10:00) (p_evening = p_morning)
two_prop_z_test.alt_hypothesis: H1: The proportion of delayed flights differs significantly between evening and morning (p_evening != p_morning)
two_prop_z_test.conclusion: Evening peak departures experience a significantly higher delay rate than morning flights due to network cascade delays.

chi_square_test.name: Chi-Square Test of Independence (Weather Severity vs Flight Outcome)
chi_square_test.null_hypothesis: H0: Flight outcome (On-Time, Delayed, Cancelled) is independent of weather severity category
chi_square_test.alt_hypothesis: H1: Flight outcome is dependent on weather severity category

anova_test.name: One-Way ANOVA (Arrival Delay Discrepancies Across Major Airlines)
anova_test.null_hypothesis: H0: Mean arrival delay duration is identical across carriers (mu_AA = mu_DL = mu_UA = mu_WN = mu_B6)
anova_test.alt_hypothesis: H1: At least one carrier has a significantly different mean arrival delay duration
anova_test.conclusion: Statistically significant variance in delay durations exists across primary carriers.

correlation_analysis.name: Correlation Analysis (Departure Delay Propagation to Arrival Delay)
correlation_analysis.interpretation: Extremely strong positive correlation showing ground departure delays propagate almost 1:1 into destination arrival delays.
